Adverse media (2025-04-08): Bank of Lithuania fined Revolut EUR 3.5m, its largest ever, for AML monitoring shortcomings (set against Revolut Holdings Europe revenues); Revolut settled and said no confirmed money laundering was identified

Adverse media (Sept/Oct 2023): FCA/NCA scrutiny of Revolut's UK e-money operation over alleged withdrawals from NCA-flagged suspicious accounts; FT estimated up to £1.7m released in July–August 2023, Revolut said £500,000; reported probe, not an adjudicated breach; no public enforcement outcome found

Adverse media (2023-03-01): auditor BDO could not verify £477m of Revolut Ltd's £636m 2021 revenues; FRC earlier called the 2020 audit 'inadequate'; delayed UK banking licence; CFO Mikko Salovaara left May 2023

Adverse media (2026-07-10): Lithuania's FNTT said Revolut accounts for ~80% of suspicious transaction reports in Lithuania (about 80,000 of ~100,000), mostly potential fraud; Revolut cited scale and AI monitoring; no enforcement action announced

Adverse media (2025-12): FT reported Revolut did not inform UK regulators in advance of a Companies House filing listing CEO Nikolay Storonsky as a UAE resident; later amended as an 'administrative error'
Adverse media (2025-11): Revolut criticised for freezing accounts of Russian expatriates in Europe, which it said was to comply with EU sanctions against Russia

Adverse media (2019-04-01, high): BBC reported whistleblower allegations about AML controls at Revolut's UK e-money business and temporary disabling of an automatic transaction-halting mechanism for potential sanctions matches; FCA enquiries resulted in requirements for specific actions; Revolut disputed the allegations; no money laundering or sanctions evasion finding established

Adverse media (2024-06-04, medium): Larsson v Revolut Limited – fraud victim's contract, negligence and dishonest assistance claims; contract and tort claims struck out, dishonest-assistance claim could proceed only if repleaded; interlocutory judgment, no finding of dishonesty

Adverse media (2024-06-12, medium): Terna Energy Trading doo v Revolut Ltd – unjust-enrichment claim after fraudulent payment; Revolut's strike-out/summary-judgment application dismissed, trial required; permission to appeal later granted; final disposition unverified

Adverse media (2024-10-14, high): BBC Panorama reported customer allegations of account-security failures and disputed reimbursement involving Revolut's UK e-money business; not a regulatory fine or judicial finding of fraud

Adverse media (2024-10-19, medium): BBC reported more than 100 customers contacted it after scams involving Revolut accounts; one customer lost £39,000; an employer was pursuing a Financial Ombudsman Service matter
Adverse media (2025-10, medium): BBC reported an ombudsman decided in favour of a business-account scam victim; Revolut reimbursed the loss and paid compensation; no broader enforcement finding

Adverse media (2026-09-12, medium): Reuters reported Revolut confirmed sensitive customer information was disclosed to an unauthorized third party after fraudulent requests using a legitimate government-agency email domain; very limited customer group, affected customers notified, regulators alerted

c24.note: OpenSanctions shows Storonsky is not on a sanctions list and has a sanctioned relative of the same name. Search coverage confirms Ukraine sanctioned the father on 19 Oct 2022, but I could not open the Telegraph piece. I found no confirmation of the Gazprom Promgaz dates (deputy 1999–2019, CEO from Dec 2019) or the PEP framing.

c25.note: Born in Dolgoprudny, Russia. News reports say he renounced Russian citizenship in 2022, though Revolut says it happened earlier, and the timing is disputed.

c26.note: The search shows only Revolut Payments Australia Pty Ltd. It appears in the BIC and FATCA datasets, which are not sanctions lists. No designation appears.

c27.note: The Storonsky profile says he has not been found on international sanctions lists, and the Revolut search shows no UK-list hits. I did not directly query Revolut Group Holdings Ltd. The page flags a possible sanctioned namesake record (Q85939911), which looks like a name-matching artifact.

c28.note: The page lists no EU sanctions dataset for Storonsky. The 'Sanction-linked' topic is inferred by graph tagging, not a designation, as the claim says.

c29.note: The fine is real (EUR 3.5m, 8 Apr 2025) but was imposed on Revolut Bank UAB, the Lithuanian bank. It was not imposed on the UK entity Revolut Ltd, so it should be excluded as a different entity, or attributed to the group only.

c30.note: The article confirms an FCA/NCA review of up to £1.7M released from flagged accounts. It is paywalled and the Revolut £500k response was not visible. The claim's description of it as an unadjudicated probe fits the article.

c31.note: Reuters was blocked and the fetch failed. Secondary reports confirm BDO could not verify £477m of the £636m 2021 revenue, the FRC called the 2020 audit inadequate, and CFO Salovaara later left. I did not check the May 2023 date.

c32.note: The article, dated 10 July 2026, matches the claim: the FNTT head said about 80% of roughly 100,000 STRs came from Revolut, mostly potential fraud. The page does not mention AI monitoring, and it notes a separate €3.5m Bank of Lithuania AML fine from last year.

c33.note: Wikipedia cites the December 2025 FT report. Revolut did not tell UK regulators in advance of a filing listing Storonsky as a UAE resident, and the filing was later amended as an 'administrative error'.

c34.note: Wikipedia reports that in November 2025 Revolut was criticised for freezing Russian expatriates' accounts, which it said was needed to comply with EU sanctions.

c35.note: The BBC piece (1 April 2019) covers a 2016 whistleblower's AML and compliance concerns and says the FCA required specific actions. I found no mention in it of a disabled sanctions mechanism, which came from the Telegraph in March 2019. Because the claim attributes that to the BBC, I marked it false.

c36.note: The 4 June 2024 judgment by Zacaroli J struck out the contract and tort claims. The dishonest-assistance claim was not struck out. I could only read search summaries, because bailii returned 403/Anubis. The claim says the claim could proceed 'only if repleaded', and the summaries did not confirm that detail.

c37.note: Revolut's strike-out/summary-judgment application was dismissed and the €700k unjust-enrichment claim went to trial. This is an interlocutory ruling, and the claim itself says the final outcome is unverified. I did not confirm the later permission to appeal.

c38.note: The Panorama investigation aired around 14 Oct 2024 and is corroborated by the 19 Oct BBC follow-up and secondary coverage. The BBC page itself would not load. The claim itself says it is not a fine or a finding of fraud, so the 'high' severity looks overstated. Medium would fit better.

c39.note: The BBC article dated 19 Oct 2024 confirms more than 100 people contacted the BBC and that Dr Ravi Kumar lost £39k. I did not read as far as the employer's Financial Ombudsman Service matter.

c40.note: The BBC page returned 'Service Temporarily Unavailable' and WebFetch was blocked. Two searches found no confirmation of an October 2025 ombudsman decision, reimbursement or compensation.

c41.note: I couldn't open the Reuters page, because the fetch was blocked. TechCrunch, Khaleej Times (which carries the same headline as the Reuters piece) and The Register all report the same incident on 2026-09-12. Revolut confirmed a limited number of customers were affected and said it notified them and alerted regulators. Medium severity is reasonable. The coverage doesn't say which Revolut entity was involved, so I assumed the main operating company.

c1.note: Companies House lists the company name as 'Revolut Ltd' (stored as REVOLUT LTD in the officer records). Company no. 08804411, active, incorporated 6 Dec 2013.

c9.note: The active officers list shows Yatsenko as a Director appointed 11 Aug 2017, British nationality. The CTO/co-founder role is not on the register page, but it is widely known.

c18.note: The PSC register shows Revolut Group Holdings Ltd (12743269) as active, notified 29 Apr 2022, with 75%+ of shares and voting rights. Nikolay Storonsky ceased as a PSC on 29 Apr 2022.

c22.note: Companies House shows REVOLUT TRADING LTD, no. 11567840, active, incorporated 13 Sep 2018.

c26.note: OpenSanctions search for 'Revolut Ltd' returned one result: Revolut Payments Australia Pty Ltd, from the BIC and FATCA lists only, with no sanctions. No match for Revolut Ltd.

c31.note: The Reuters page itself could not be loaded (the fetch failed with a server error). Kitco's copy of the Reuters story, City AM and Bloomberg confirm BDO could not verify £477m of £636m in 2021 revenue. In 2022 the FRC criticised BDO's 2020 audit of Revolut. The CFO's May 2023 exit is confirmed by PYMNTS, but it came after the 1 Mar 2023 article.

c39.note: The BBC article confirms more than 100 people came forward, an NHS consultant lost £39k, and an employer's case is with the Financial Ombudsman. The 19 Oct 2024 date was not checked directly, but it fits the Panorama broadcast on 14 Oct 2024.
